We require,0.1 molar ferric chloride (0.1 M FeCl₃) solution,0.1 molar potassium thiocyanate (0.1 M KCNS) solution,0.1 molar potassium chloride (0.1 M KCl) solution, distilled water, four test tubes labelled A, B, C, and D, test tube rack,
A clean 250 ml beaker, and measuring cylinders.
Take 10 ml of 0.1 M FeCl₃ solution in a measuring cylinder.
Pour it into the 250 ml beaker.
Take 10 ml of 0.1M KCNS solution in another measuring cylinder.
Pour it into the beaker containing FeCl₃ solution. A deep red colour is obtained due to the formation of ferric - thiocyanate complex, [Fe(SCN)(H₂O)₅]²⁺.
Take 50 ml of distilled water in a measuring cylinder.
Pour it into the beaker containing ferric - thiocyanate complex, to dilute the solution.
Take 10 ml of the above solution in a measuring cylinder.
Take the test tube labelled as 'A'.
Pour the solution into the test tube.
Take another 10 ml solution in the measuring cylinder.
Take the test tube labelled as 'B' and pour the solution into it.
Repeat the same process for the other two test tubes.
Take 5ml of distilled water in a measuring cylinder.
Add it into the test tube “A” and shake the test tube well. The Colour of the solution in this test is taken as the reference colour.
Take 5ml of 0.1M FeCl₃ solution in the measuring cylinder.

Add it into the test tube, “B” and shake the test tube well. The colour of the solution deepens because the increase in concentration of Fe³⁺ ions results in more ferric - thiocyanate complex and shifts the equilibrium in the forward direction.
Take 5 ml of 0.1M KCNS solution in the measuring cylinder.

Add it to the test tube, “C” and shake the test tube well. The colour of the solution deepens because the increase in concentration of SCN⁻ ions results in more ferric - thiocyanate complex and shifts the equilibrium in the forward direction.
Similarly, take 5ml of 0.1M KCl solution in another measuring cylinder.
Add it to the test tube, "D" and shake the test tube well.

The colour of the solution becomes lighter because the increase in concentration of K⁺ ions decreases the concentration of SCN⁻ ions and thus decreases the concentration of complex. Thus the equilibrium shifts in the backward direction.
Now compare the intensity of the colours in test tubes B, C, and D with the red colour in test tube A,taken as the reference colour.

Now compare the intensity of the colours in test tubes B, C, and D with the red colour in test tube A,taken as the reference colour.
Record the observations in a tabular column. The equilibrium between Fe³⁺ ions and SCN⁻ ions is directly proportional to the concentration of the reactants.
